We are Team ENTROPY, a group of Computer Science students. We know the basics of Java and OOP, and we can build websites. We enjoy learning new skills, solving problems, and working together.

We are excited to join the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to use our skills and ideas to build a useful and creative project using NASA's data. We hope to learn new things, share ideas, and gain new experience as a team.
summary:
**ENTROPY: ZERO** is an interactive, educational space mission simulation game developed by **ENTROPY Team** for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project transforms complex space engineering concepts into an engaging, accessible, and realistic learning experience.

Players take on the role of space mission engineers, designing and managing missions to **Earth, the Moon, and Mars**. They select spacecraft components, choose rockets and orbits, and make critical engineering decisions. Through interactive simulations, players experience how their choices affect mission success or failure, encouraging problem-solving, critical thinking, and learning through experimentation.

The project also celebrates **Saudi Arabia's contributions to space exploration**, highlighting the historic journey of Prince Sultan bin Salman in 1985 and Rayyanah Barnawi's mission in 2023.

By combining NASA scientific resources, interactive simulations, and immersive storytelling, ENTROPY: ZERO bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application.

Our goal is to **make space science accessible to everyone, inspire the next generation of explorers, and turn curiosity about space into real scientific understanding.**

ENTROPY: ZERO — Project Details

Project Overview

ENTROPY: ZERO is an interactive, web-based space mission simulation game developed by ENTROPY Team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, immersive, and educational experience.

Instead of simply reading about space exploration, users become mission engineers who design spacecraft, make critical decisions, simulate missions, and discover how engineering choices influence mission outcomes.

Our vision is to make space science understandable, engaging, and accessible to students, beginners, and future space explorers.

How Does It Work?

ENTROPY: ZERO guides players through an interactive mission design process:

1. Mission Selection

Players choose between three space exploration missions with different difficulty levels:

  • Earth Observation (Easy): Design a satellite mission to observe Earth.
  • Lunar Exploration (Medium): Develop a mission focused on studying the Moon.
  • Mars Exploration (Hard): Face more advanced challenges associated with exploring Mars.

2. Spacecraft Design

Players select spacecraft components and scientific equipment while considering mission requirements, mass, power, and engineering constraints.

3. Rocket and Orbit Selection

Players choose a launch vehicle and orbital configuration appropriate for their mission objectives.

4. Mission Simulation

The simulation evaluates the player's engineering decisions and demonstrates how different configurations influence mission performance.

5. Mission Results and Analysis

Players receive feedback on mission success or failure, helping them understand engineering trade-offs, identify problems, and improve future designs.

This process encourages experimentation, logical reasoning, and learning through practical decision-making.

Technologies and Tools Used

Our team developed ENTROPY: ZERO using modern web development technologies:

  • React.js: Building the interactive user interface and game components.
  • JavaScript: Implementing mission logic, engineering calculations, and simulation functionality.
  • Vite: Providing a fast development and build environment.
  • CSS: Creating responsive layouts, visual effects, and a futuristic interface.
  • React Three Fiber / Three.js: Supporting interactive 3D space visualizations.
  • GitHub: Managing source code, collaboration, and version control.
  • Visual Studio Code: Developing and maintaining the application.

We also referenced scientific and educational resources from NASA, including the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), NASA 3D Resources, and NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS).

Our project is designed to run in a web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes ENTROPY: ZERO unique is its combination of space engineering, interactive simulation, cinematic storytelling, and educational gameplay.

Rather than presenting space science as static information, our platform allows users to experience the consequences of their own engineering decisions.

The project also integrates Saudi Arabia's space exploration heritage, highlighting Prince Sultan bin Salman's historic 1985 spaceflight and Rayyanah Barnawi's 2023 mission to the International Space Station.

This connection between scientific education and real-world achievements creates a meaningful experience that inspires users to imagine themselves contributing to future space missions.
